rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command means full outward and inward faith in the Prophet, this revelation, and earlier revelation; merely saying one believes in God and the Last Day is insufficient.
rows.anchor: Peygamber’e ve ona inzal edilene ve ondan evvel inzal edilene dahi zâhiren ve bâtınen, kalben ve lisânen iman ediniz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sefih linguistically means lightness and thinness of judgment from deficient reason, lack of thought or steadiness; religiously it is acting against reason and religion, the opposite of sound guidance.
rows.anchor: Lügaten “sefeh”, re’y ü revişte hafiflik ve yufkalıktır ki akıl noksanından neş’et eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sefeh is following whim and appetite rather than reason; it may arise from innate foolishness or from reason becoming ineffectual, which is how hypocrites use the word.
rows.anchor: re’y u fikirde heva vü hevese tâbi‘olmak, akıl ile değil zevk ile hareket etmektir

rows.speaker: İmam Vâhidî
rows.claim: Al-Wahidi answers that the hypocrites said this among themselves, not in front of believers, and God reports their private speech.
rows.anchor: İmam Vâhidî buna cevâben “Bunlar bu sözü mü’minler arasında değil, aralarında izhar ediyorlardı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Wahidi's explanation conflicts with the apparent syntax, which places the saying at the same time as the instruction; interpreting it as an unspoken thought also departs from the apparent sense.
rows.anchor: Lâkin bu, zâhir-i siyâka muhaliftir. Çünkü “قِيلَ,”إِذَا ile قَالُوٓا۟’nun aynı zamanda vukū‘unu iktizâ ediyor

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase is a deliberately two-faced, hypocritical insinuation, so even when spoken to advisers it need not be an unequivocal public declaration of unbelief; it resembles their phrase in 4:46.
rows.anchor: bu söz tam münafıkça ikiyüzlü, tevriyeli bir söz olduğundan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The contrast between hypocrites and al-nas is pointed: they imagine themselves an enlightened superior class, while the command implies that believers are more fully human and that accepting equal faith is advancement.
rows.anchor: Siz henüz insan değilsiniz, insan olunuz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They insult ordinary believers as fools and reject equal standing in faith without plainly saying they refuse faith; they imply that their own supposedly special faith deserves distinction.
rows.anchor: kendilerinin husûsî ve başka bir imanları olduğunu ve olması lâzım geldiğini ima etmek istiyorlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Arabic, al-nas can signal either honor or contempt according to context.
rows.anchor: lisân-ı Arab’da da النَّاس tâbiri makamına göre kâh tâzim ve kâh tahkir mânasını ifade eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hypocrites treat faith as a restraint for common people: they shed even its language around unbelievers and profess it among believers, while claiming elite faith differs; Islam makes belief and its conditions universal, with distinctions only in deeds and degrees of perfection.
rows.anchor: asl-ı imanda ve şerâitinde havâss u avam farkı mevzû‘-i bahis olamaz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The doubters regard purity of heart and sincerity as foolish and believers as gullible, but God declares the hypocrites themselves to be the fools, though they do not know it.
rows.anchor: süfehâ, budala ancak o münafıkların kendileridir, lâkin bilmezler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their claim to knowledge is empty: knowledge requires certainty and sound inference, especially about the future, begins in faith in God and aims at meeting Him; the successive denials of awareness and then knowledge intensify the rebuke and distinguish knowledge from perception.
rows.anchor: burada da لَّا يَعْلَمُونَ diye ilimleri nefy olunmuştur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When meeting believers the hypocrites say they believe, flatter those they consider foolish, and feign sincere loyalty.
rows.anchor: mü’minlere yaltaklanır, yüzden hulûskârlık, mürâîlik ederler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their 'satans' are rebellious, scheming teachers and leaders who make secret pacts and privately teach sedition and corruption; the hypocrites assure them they are allies.
rows.anchor: kendilerine gizli gizli fitne [237] ve fesad dersi veren

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They answer any concern about their dealings with believers by saying they are only mockers, proudly admitting treachery; these verses ground the general rule that contemptuous mockery of faith and doctrine entails unbelief.
rows.anchor: ilim ve akaidde istihfaf ve istihzânın mûcib-i küfr olması hakkındaki kā‘ide-i külliye bu gibi âyetlerin mazmûnudur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One report says Abdullah b. Ubay went out with followers, called the approaching Companions fools, then welcomed Abu Bakr, Umar, and Ali with lavish honorific praise before the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: Rivayet olunduğuna göre Abdullah b. Übey yardaklarıyla bir gün sokağa çıkmışlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fuller version says Ali rebuked Ibn Ubay, who claimed their faith matched the Muslims'; he then told his companions to act likewise, they praised him, and Muslims informed the Messenger before the verse descended.
rows.anchor: Müsaade et yâ Ebe’l-Hasen benim hakkımda böyle mi söylüyorsun? Vallahi bizim imanımız sizin imanınız gibi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In that report, Ibn Ubay is the one who says 'we believe,' representing his companions; the earlier singular wording supports this reading.
rows.anchor: “âmennâ” diyen esasen İbn Übey b. Selûl oluyor ve bu sözle arkadaşlarını da temsil ediyor

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural satans are a group distinct from Ibn Ubay and the hypocrites, linked to them through a concealed organization; the verse reveals a deeper, hidden source of the incident.
rows.anchor: bu şeytanların gürûh-ı münâfıkīnin arkasında ve onlardan hâriç ve fakat onlarla gizli bir alâkayı hâiz hafî bir teşkilâta delâlet ettiği âşikârdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Many exegetes identify these satans beyond the hypocrite leaders as chiefs of the polytheists and Jewish scholars.
rows.anchor: birçok müfessirîn, bu şeyâtînin, reîs-i münâfıkīnden başka rüesâ-yı müşrikîne ve ahbâr-ı Yehûd’a işaret olduğunu nakletmişlerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shaytan is a common noun for any exceptionally rebellious, malicious creature, human or animal, visible or hidden; the hidden essence of human evil is known by its effects, and the term also applies to jinn and animals.
rows.anchor: insan şeytanında bile şeytanlık bir emr-i hafîdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some philosophers explain the jinn Satan as only an immaterial spiritual being, but the author follows Ahl al-Sunna in also affirming its material aspect and evil material forces.
rows.anchor: bunun maddî haysiyetini de inkâr etmek doğru olamayacağından buna habis olan maddî kuvvetleri dahi ilâve etmek zarûrîdir. Ve ehl-i sünnetin îzahı böyledir

rows.speaker: Sîbeveyh
rows.claim: One etymology derives shaytan from sh-t-n, 'distance': Satan is far from truth and must be kept far away.
rows.anchor: Sîbeveyh’in dediği gibi uzaklık mânasına شطن maddesinden فَیْعَال veznindedir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative etymology derives shaytan from a root meaning burning or invalidation, on the fa'lan pattern; on this account it is not a proper name and is declinable.
rows.anchor: Diğeri ihtirak veya butlan mânasına شیط maddesinden فَعْلَاَن vezninde olmasıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shaytan is a genus name, especially for invisible evil spirits and powers; as every kind began with a first individual, it can evoke Iblis as the progenitor and function like a proper name.
rows.anchor: bu cinsin babası olan o ferd-i evvel, yani İblis hatıra gelir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Persian word for Satan is div, which the author says reached the West and became dieu with the opposite meaning, god.
rows.anchor: Şeytana lisân-ı Fârisîde “dîv” denilir ki bu kelime garba dolaşmış, aksine ilâh mânasına “dieu” olmuştur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author recounts that Umar dismounted a horse in Syria after it began prancing, saying they had put him on a satan; this illustrates that the term can literally describe an animal.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Ömer Şam’a teşriflerinde bir ata bindirilmiş idi, biner binmez at çalım yapmaya başlayınca hemen inmiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Exegetes agree that the satans meant in this verse are human satans.
rows.anchor: Bu âyette ise insan şeytanları olduğunda müfessirînin ihtilâfı görülmüyor

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seventh verse succinctly summarizes the hypocrites' character and psychology, elaborating the opening description of them among people and compressing their whole spirit into two words of their own confession.
rows.anchor: onların bütün rûhlarını kendi ikrarlarıyla iki kelimede hulâsa ederek gösterivermiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although hearers may demand the hypocrites' immediate destruction, God calms them: divine mockery exposes the hypocrites and lets them continue wandering blindly in rebellion.
rows.anchor: bütün bu heyecânı teskin ve endişeleri izâle etmek için derhâl buyuruyor ki

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's worldly mockery includes treating hypocrites as Muslims under Islamic worship and civil law, rather than excluding them like open non-Muslims; believers must enforce those rules. This shows Islam's patience, may nurture believing children, and makes hypocrites suffer under rules they disbelieve.
rows.anchor: Münafıklara gerek ibâdât ve gerek mu‘âmelâta müte‘allik ahkâm-ı ilâhiyenin hepsi Müslümanlar gibi tatbik edilir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hypocrites also face mockery in the afterlife: they are in the lowest level of the Fire, and hadith reports describe Paradise's gates being shown to them and then shut.
rows.anchor: cennetin kapıları kendilerine gösterilip gösterilip de kapatılıvereceği hadislerde beyan olunmuştur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling God 'Allah' in the third person instead of using 'I' or 'we' displays majesty and grandeur, as when a commander says 'your commander wants this' rather than 'I want this.'
rows.anchor: izhâr-ı celâl ve kibriyâ içindir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istihza means making someone ridiculous in jest and breaking their honor; the word is associated with crushing or swift killing.
rows.anchor: “İstihza” bir kimseyi hezl içinde maskara etmek ve şeref ü haysiyetini kırmak istemektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For divine acts, the ultimate purpose is intended; God's istihza is not frivolous joking but just humiliation that exposes and disgraces offenders while they imagine they are concealing their faults and remain unaware.
rows.anchor: adâlet-i ilâhiyesini izhar etmek için böyle bir tahkir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human mockers often fail to humiliate their targets and become ridiculous themselves; God's mockery truly disgraces them before creation, and the author calls this divine justice, illustrated by a fool displaying a sign that says he is disgraced.
rows.anchor: Ve bütün kâinât nazarında bednâm eyler de o, bir mecnun gibi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Theologically, one should not call God 'a mocker' as a noun; the proper wording is that He performs the act of mockery.
rows.anchor: şer‘an Allah’a “müstehzî” denilmez fakat “istihza eder” denilir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hypocrites exchanged guidance, which had been within their grasp, for misguidance; their trade yields no profit and they cannot find or follow a profitable path because they lost guidance, their greatest capital.
rows.anchor: sermayelerin sermayesi olan hidâyeti vermiş yerine onun zayâ‘ı demek olan dalâleti almışlardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This verse parallels the description of the God-guided righteous in 2:5 and states the hypocrites' final condition; the trade metaphor reflects their familiar worldly concern and warns that religious guidance is prior to and necessary for sound worldly commerce.
rows.anchor: Bu âyet müttakīn hakkındaki أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ عَلَىٰ هُدًۭى مِّن رَّبِّهِمْ âyetinin ‘adîli olarak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The image praises trade while teaching that its true path is sound understanding and uprightness: lying, deception, and intrigue cannot produce real profit, and religious guidance is needed to remain honest.
rows.anchor: ticarette yalan, hud‘a, entrika yolunun hakīkī bir kâr yolu olmadığına tenbih

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because hypocrites work from within to derail Islam's aims, believers need particular warning about them; four following verses make their loss tangible through parables and deter hypocrisy.
rows.anchor: bir taraftan bunlar hakkında alenî kâfirden ziyade nazar-ı dikkati celb ile mü’minleri tenvir etmek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Breaking what God commands to be joined means failing to do righteous deeds and acting against divine commands and laws that secure rectitude; sins and major sins spread corruption on earth.
rows.anchor: Amel-i sâlih yapmazlar, salâhı temin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fisq literally means going out, as mice leaving holes are called fawasiq; religiously it means leaving obedience through major sins, including persistence in minor sins.
rows.anchor: “Fısk”, asl-ı lügatta hurûc mânasınadır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fisq has three degrees: occasional sin while recognizing its ugliness, habitual immersion in it, and committing it while denying its ugliness; only the third is unbelief.
rows.anchor: Birincisi günahı çirkin addetmekle beraber ahyânen irtikâb etmek, ikincisi üzerine düşerek inhimak ile yapmak, üçüncüsü çirkinliğini inkâr ederek yapmaktır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Sunni doctrine, a sinner retains the name believer until the unbelieving degree; Mu'tazilites place such a person between believer and unbeliever, while Kharijites call all three degrees unbelief.
rows.anchor: bu kısmı ne mü’min ne kâfir ikisi ortası

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people called transgressors here are unquestionably unbelievers because they combine covenant-breaking, rejection of divine commands, and corruption through forbidden acts; the preceding verse's disbelievers' response to the parable reinforces this.
rows.anchor: Allah’a verdiği ahdi nakz edip akidesini bozmak, emr-i ilâhînin aksini yapmak, menâhîyi irtikâb ile de yeryüzünü fesâda vermek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A key shift is that the earlier contrast was faith versus unbelief, while this passage sets faith and righteous action against fisq; rejection or misinterpretation of Quranic parables is tied to intellectual and practical aspects of transgression.
rows.anchor: yalnız iman ve küfür tekabülü esas iken burada hem iman ve hem amel-i sâlih mecmû‘una mukabil olmak üzere ayrıca da fısk

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The intellectual root of unbelief is bad interpretation, deliberate or ignorant, often directed at parables and ambiguous passages, and it usually accompanies practical unbelief; the Quran affirms parables as true and necessary to its style.
rows.anchor: temsîlâtın da mevcûdiyetini ve bunun esası olan hak nokta-i nazarına muhalif değil, belki lâzım bulunduğunu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Araf 7:53 depicts those who forgot the promised interpretation recognizing the messengers' truth only when it arrives, then finding their inventions gone and themselves lost; accept true parables, act, and let events disclose their interpretation.
rows.anchor: Binâen‘aleyh temsîlât-ı hakka inan, matlub olan ameli yap, tevilini istikbale, cereyân-ı hâdisâta bırak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fisq entails either unbelief or ingratitude and ends in loss; after condemning it in the third person, the discourse turns to direct address for guidance.
rows.anchor: Hulâsa, fısk, ya küfrü veya küfrânı mutazammındır ve neticesi hüsrandır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The losers are the whole class deprived of gain, whose work consists entirely of loss.
rows.anchor: Kazançtan mahrum, işi gücü zarar ve ziyan olan kimseler diye asıl bunlara denilir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham asks that some of his descendants, not all, share in the gift of imamate and prophethood; he knew a universal grant would conflict with wisdom by reducing their number, producing division, and making them dependent on outsiders for support.
rows.anchor: anlaşılıyor ya “hepsine” demedi, zira bilirdi ki hepsine talep, muhâlif-i hikmet olurdu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's reply excludes all unjust descendants from His covenant and makes imamate the right of the just; the verse establishes that an unjust person is unfit for leadership and a leader who later becomes unjust must be removed.
rows.anchor: Bu âyet zâlimin imamete ehil olmadığına ve ibtidâ âdil olup, sonradan zulüm yaparsa hal‘i vâcib bulunduğuna delildir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite plural 'the unjust' is general across all generations, but its immediate historical target is Israel; earlier rebukes in 2:51 and 2:92 and the surah's catalogue of their sins establish their wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ kıyamete kadar gelecek zâlimlerin hepsine şâmildir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Israel once received prophetic leadership while oppressed, but from the calf episode onward its wrongdoing became collective, ending its imamate, which passed to Abraham's other line through Ishmael.
rows.anchor: artık ba‘demâ imamet İsrâil evlâdından çıktı ve İbrâhim zürriyetinin diğer koluna geçti

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promised final prophet in the Torah would come from Ishmael's descendants, not Israel; the Israelites reject Muhammad from envy, though he belongs to Abraham's unmarked lineage and they could share the honor by accepting him.
rows.anchor: Tevrat’ta mev‘ud olan Hâtemü’l-enbiyâ İsrâil oğullarından değil

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made the Kaaba, also called the Ancient House, a destination and refuge: people visit and gain reward, while those in its sanctuary are secure from attack.
rows.anchor: Kâbe’yi vaktiyle insanlara merci‘ve me’men yapmıştık. Nâs onu hac ve ziyaret ederler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to take Abraham's Station as a prayer place means praying there or supplicating; it is the stone where Abraham stood while building the House or calling people to pilgrimage, and circumambulation prayer is performed there.
rows.anchor: “Makām-ı İbrâhim”, İbrâhim aleyhisselâm’ın Beyt’i bina ederken veyahut nâsı hacca davet ederken üzerine çıktığı taşın bulunduğu yerdir

rows.speaker: Nâfi‘ ve İbn Âmir
rows.claim: These readers have the past-tense reading 'they took'; people had made the Kaaba their qibla before the direction changed from Bayt al-Maqdis, so the verse also encourages the qibla transfer.
rows.anchor: Nâfi‘ve İbn Âmir kıraatlerinde mâzi sîgasıyla وَاتَّخَذُوا okunur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God firmly commanded Abraham and Ishmael to keep the House pure for circumambulating pilgrims, residents or those in retreat, and people bowing and prostrating; they were to maintain its purity constantly.
rows.anchor: beytimi tavaf edenler, mücaveret eyleyen veya i‘tikâfa girenler, rükû sücûd yapanlar, namaz kılanlar için temizleyiniz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because ritual bowing in prayer is particular to Muhammad's community, this covenant foretold to Abraham and Ishmael that such a community would come.
rows.anchor: Rükû ile namaz yalnız ümmet-i Muhammed’e mahsus olduğuna nazaran Cenâb-ı Allah bu ahidde Hazret-i İbrâhim ve İsmâil’e böyle bir ümmetin geleceğini bildirmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham's prayer for Mecca's safety and produce arose when he first left Hajar and Ishmael in the barren valley; Hajar accepted the situation after learning God had commanded it, and Abraham prayed from Kedā, as also related at 14:37.
rows.anchor: İbrâhim aleyhisselâm İsmâil ile Hâcer’i buraya bırakıp Şam’a döndüğü zaman

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham asks provision specifically for believers, but God says He provides for disbelievers too, granting them only brief worldly enjoyment before compelling them to the Fire and a wretched end.
rows.anchor: hem ona hem de kâfir olana rızık veririm

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham had analogized sustenance to imamate and prayed to restrict it to believers; God corrects him because worldly provision is mercy for believers and disbelievers alike, unlike imamate, a precedence in religion and worldly affairs.
rows.anchor: rızık mü’min ve kâfire şâmil bir rahmet-i dünyeviye olduğundan bunun hem din ve hem dünyada takaddüm demek olan imamete kıyası ma‘a’l-fârik

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The correction shows that even prophets may err in analogy and independent reasoning, with God correcting them immediately; analogy is therefore not a firm proof in divine matters.
rows.anchor: enbiyânın kıyas ve içtihadında bile hata olabiliyor ve fakat Allah onların hatasını derhâl tashih buyuruyor

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As Abraham and Ishmael raise the Kaaba's foundations, they ask God to accept their humble work because He hears their prayer and knows their intentions.
rows.anchor: Ey Rabbimiz bârigâh-ı ehadiyetine ref‘ettiğimiz âcizâne fiillerimizi bizden kabul et

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When 'Islam' takes a lam complement as in this prayer, it means or includes complete surrender, obedience, and compliance.
rows.anchor: nefs, itaat ve inkıyâd-ı kâmil mânasına gelir veya onu tazammun eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prayer asks for a Muslim community from their descendants and for guidance to the places of worship and sacrifice; manasik is plural of mansak, while nusuk originally means utmost devotion and became common for pilgrimage and sacrifice.
rows.anchor: نُسُك fi’l-asl son derece ta‘abbüddür. Fakat hac ve kurban hakkında şâyi‘dir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their request for repentance seeks acceptance for them all and God's continuing regard; He alone is the Ever-Relenting and Merciful.
rows.anchor: Ve bizim hepimize tevbeler nasib et ve tevbelerimizi kabul eyle, bize bir kere değil dâima nazar et

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The requested messenger will recite God's signs, teach scripture and wisdom, and purify the people; wisdom means mastery in knowledge and action, accuracy in speech and deed, a topic developed at 2:269.
rows.anchor: Asl-ı “hikmet”, ilm ü amelde itkan, ta‘bîr-i âharla kavl ü fiilde isabet demektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The messenger is Muhammad, since no other prophet from Ishmael's descendants is agreed upon; his hadith identifies him as Abraham's prayer, Jesus' good news, and his mother's vision.
rows.anchor: Bu resulden murad da Hâtemü’l-enbiyâ Muhammed Mustafâ sallâllahu aleyhi ve sellem olduğu âşikârdır

rows.speaker: Resûlullah
rows.claim: The Prophet says he is the prayer of his father Abraham, the glad tidings of his brother Jesus, and his mother's vision.
rows.anchor: أَنَا دَعْوَةُ أَبِي إِبْرَاهِيمَ، وَبُشْرَى أخي عِيسَى وَرُؤْيَا أُمِّي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As thanks for Abraham's prayer, Muhammad's community was taught to invoke blessings on Muhammad and his family as God blessed Abraham and his family; these verses clarify the meaning and basis of that comparison.
rows.anchor: bu duasına şükrâne olmak üzeredir ki ümmet-i Muhammed’e de namazlarda

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham and Ishmael's prayer while laying the Kaaba's foundations asks that the promised imamate culminate in a Muslim community from Abraham's descendants and a noble messenger among them; Muhammad's mission fulfills the prayer.
rows.anchor: bu dualar bi‘set-i Muhammediye ile tamam olmuştur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taken together, the exclusion of wrongdoers from imamate, the Kaaba and Mecca, Ishmael's line, the Muslim community, and the messenger's teaching and purification should remove any doubt among people of scripture about Muhammad's mission and Islam as Abraham's religion.
rows.anchor: risâlet-i Muhammediye ve millet-i İbrâhim olan dîn-i İslâm hakkında cidden ehl-i kitab bulunanların hiç şüphesi kalmaz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To turn from Abraham's milla, the communal spirit of Islam, is irrational; only someone who debases himself and wants continued subjugation would forfeit the promised felicity.
rows.anchor: Hangi akıl sâhibi bundan istinkâf eder de onun zürriyetine mev‘ud olan bu saadetten mahrum kalmak ister

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Abdullah b. Salam invited his nephews Salama and Muhajir to Islam, citing the Torah's promise of Ahmad from Ishmael's descendants; Salama accepted Islam while Muhajir refused, and the verse then descended.
rows.anchor: Rivayet olunuyor ki Abdullah b. Selâm biraderzâdeleri Seleme ile Muhacir’i İslâm’a davet etmiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God selected Abraham in this world as a refined and purified exemplar, choosing him for supreme imamate, prophethood, and wisdom, and he will belong to the righteous in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: Biz o azamet-i şânımızla İbrâhim’i dünyada ıstıfâ ettik, yani sâir halk arasından bir zübde-i sâfiye olarak seçtik

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham's selection began when God first commanded him to submit and he surrendered himself to the Lord of the worlds.
rows.anchor: Rabbi ona, “arz-ı islâm et, Bana ihlâs u iman ile teslim ol” dediği ilk ân-ı teklîfte

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The initial command to submit reflects God's showing Abraham signs of oneness through the setting of stars, moon, and sun; before prophethood and puberty he reasoned to the Creator and testified to pure monotheism, never having been a polytheist.
rows.anchor: yıldızların, kamerin, şemsin ufûlünden Hâlık teâlâ’ya ve vahdâniyetine istidlâli ihtar eylemiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islam was Abraham's religion from the beginning, and both he and his grandson Jacob enjoined it upon their sons; Nafi, Ibn Amir, and Abu Ja'far read the verb as 'they enjoined.'
rows.anchor: Nâfi‘, İbn Âmir, Ebû Ca‘fer kıraatlerinde وَوَصَّىٰ بِهَآ okunur ki vasiyet ettiler demek olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham's sons were Ishmael, Isaac, Midian, and Medan, with other reports giving eight or twenty-four; Jacob had twelve sons, listed here, whose descendants are the Children of Israel.
rows.anchor: İbrâhim’in oğulları: İsmâil, İshâk, Medyen, Medan dört idi. Sekiz veya yirmi dört rivayeti de vardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fathers tell their sons that God chose for them the purest and most excellent religion to follow, so they must die only as complete Muslims.
rows.anchor: Cenâb-ı Allah her hâlde sizin için ittibâ‘olunacak dini bizzat ıstıfâ ve intihab etti
